questions.question: Who presides over the Rajya Sabha in the absence of the vice-president?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 89** of the **Indian Constitution**, the **Vice-President of India** is the **ex-officio Chairman** of the **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• In the **absence** of the **Chairman**, the **Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha** presides over the sittings of the House as per **Article 91**.
 
• The **Deputy Chairman** is elected by the members of the **Rajya Sabha** from among themselves; unlike the **Chairman**, they must be a member of the House.
 
• While acting as the **presiding officer**, the **Deputy Chairman** possesses all the powers and duties of the **Chairman**, including the power to maintain **decorum** and the right to exercise a **casting vote** in case of a tie.
 
• It is important to note that the **Deputy Chairman** is not subordinate to the **Chairman**; they are directly responsible to the **Rajya Sabha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Speaker of Lok Sabha**:

 
 
• The **Speaker** is the **presiding officer** of the **Lower House** (Lok Sabha).
 
• In a **joint sitting** of both Houses of **Parliament**, the **Speaker** presides, and in their absence, the **Deputy Speaker** or the **Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha** takes the chair.
 
 
 
• **President**:
 
 
• The **President** is the **Executive Head** of the **Union** but does not preside over either House.
 
• If the offices of both **Chairman** and **Deputy Chairman** are **vacant**, the **President** appoints a member of the **Rajya Sabha** to perform the duties of the **Chairman**.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister**:
 
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the **Head of the Council of Ministers** and the leader of the House (if they are a member of that House).
 
• They do not hold a **constitutional role** in presiding over the parliamentary sessions.
 
 
 
• **Panel of Vice-Chairpersons**:
 
 
• The **Chairman** nominates a panel of **Vice-Chairpersons** who can preside over the **Rajya Sabha** when both the **Chairman** and **Deputy Chairman** are **absent**.

questions.question: What are Boliyan in the context of Giddha dance?

options.text: Types of costumes worn by dancers
Traditional songs sung during the dance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Traditional songs sung during the dance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boliyan** (singular: Boli) are the rhythmic folk couplets or verses that form the lyrical foundation of the **Giddha** dance, a premier folk art performed by women in the **Punjab** region.
 
• These songs are traditionally transmitted through oral tradition and are central to the performance, as the dancers move and clap in synchronization with the rhythm and meaning of the lyrics.
 
• During a performance, a lead woman typically recites the **Boli**, and as the narrative reaches its peak or **Tappa**, the other dancers join in with high-pitched vocals and vigorous movements.
 
• The themes of **Boliyan** are diverse, covering various facets of Punjabi life including **social issues**, **agricultural cycles**, **family dynamics**, and emotional expressions of love, joy, or satire.
 
• Historically, these songs served as a medium for women to voice their perspectives on domestic life, often using humor to critique the **Saas-Bahu** (mother-in-law and daughter-in-law) relationship or to celebrate weddings and festivals like **Teeyan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Giddha Dance Characteristics**:

 
 
• It is considered the feminine counterpart to **Bhangra** and is known for its grace, speed, and spontaneous energy.
 
• The dance is usually performed in a circle, and unlike many other folk dances, it does not strictly require musical instruments, as rhythmic **clapping** (Thapi) provides the primary beat.
 
• Costumes for **Giddha** include vibrant **Salwar Kameez** or **Lehengas** paired with **Phulkari** (traditional embroidery) dupattas and heavy jewelry like **Suggi-Phul**.
 
 
 
• **Musical Elements**:
 
 
• While the human voice is the main component, sometimes a **Dhol** (drum) or a **Ghara** (earthen pot) is used to enhance the rhythm.
 
• The **Boliyan** are distinct from the dance steps themselves, which involve mimicking daily activities like churning milk or spinning a **Charkha**.

questions.question: Which Indian lake is of volcanic origin?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lonar Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lonar Lake** is situated in the **Buldhana district** of **Maharashtra** and is uniquely characterized as a **crater lake** formed within the **Deccan Traps**, which is a large **volcanic igneous province**.
 
• While modern geological studies confirm it was created by a **meteorite impact** approximately 52,000 years ago during the **Pleistocene Epoch**, it is categorized as a lake of volcanic origin in many contexts because it is the only known impact crater in the world formed in **basaltic rock**.
 
• The lake is **endorheic**, meaning it has no outflow, leading to high levels of **salinity** and **alkalinity** (pH levels reaching up to 10.5).
 
• It was designated as a **Ramsar site** in **November 2020**, identifying it as a wetland of international importance.
 
• The lake gained global attention in 2020 when its water turned **pink** due to the presence of **Haloarchaea**, a salt-loving microbial population.
 
• It is protected as a **National Geo-heritage Monument** by the **Geological Survey of India** (GSI).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sambhar Lake**:

 
 
• Located in **Rajasthan**, it is the largest **inland salt lake** in India.
 
• It is a **Ramsar site** and a major source of India's salt production.
 
 
 
• **Loktak Lake**:
 
 
• Located in **Manipur**, it is the largest **freshwater lake** in Northeast India.
 
• It is famous for **Phumdis** (heterogeneous mass of vegetation) and the **Keibul Lamjao National Park**, the world's only floating national park.
 
 
 
• **Chilika Lake**:
 
 
• Situated in **Odisha**, it is the largest **brackish water lagoon** in India.
 
• It was the first Indian wetland to be designated under the **Ramsar Convention** in 1981 and hosts **Irrawaddy dolphins**.

questions.question: Who was the only person to be elected president of India as an independent candidate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**V. V. Giri**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Varahagiri Venkata Giri**, popularly known as **V. V. Giri**, served as the **fourth President of India** from **24 August 1969** to **24 August 1974**.
 
• He holds the unique distinction of being the only person in the history of the **Republic of India** to be elected as an **Independent candidate** for the post of President.
 
• The **1969 Presidential Election** was a turning point in Indian politics; although the official **Indian National Congress** candidate was **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**, the then Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi** supported Giri.
 
• Giri won the election after a famous call for a **conscience vote** by **Indira Gandhi**, which led to a narrow victory over the party's official nominee and eventually caused a split in the **Congress Party**.
 
• Prior to his full term, he served as the **Vice-President of India** and became the **Acting President** following the sudden demise of **Dr. Zakir Husain** in **May 1969**.
 
• He was a prominent **trade union leader** and served as the **Union Minister of Labour**, besides holding various gubernatorial positions in states like **Uttar Pradesh**, **Kerala**, and **Mysore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neelam Sanjiva Reddy**:

 
 
• He served as the **sixth President of India** (1977–1982) and is the only person to be elected **unopposed** to the office.
 
• He also served as the **Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh** and the **Speaker of the Lok Sabha**.
 
 
 
• **Zail Singh**:
 
 
• He was the **seventh President of India** (1982–1987) and the first **Sikh** to hold the highest constitutional office.
 
• He is noted for using his **pocket veto** power against the **Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill** in 1986.
 
 
 
• **Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed**:
 
 
• He was the **fifth President of India** (1974–1977) and the second President to **die in office**.
 
• His presidency is notably associated with the signing of the **Proclamation of Emergency** in **June 1975**.

questions.question: What is the standard court size for women in Kabaddi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**12m × 8m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The standard dimensions for a **Kabaddi** court intended for **Women** and **Junior Boys** are **12 meters** in length and **8 meters** in width, as mandated by the **International Kabaddi Federation (IKF)**.
 
• The court is divided into two equal halves by a **midline**, resulting in two playing areas each measuring **6 meters × 8 meters**.
 
• The **Baulk Line** in the women’s court is marked at a distance of **3 meters** from the midline on both sides.
 
• The **Bonus Line** is situated **1 meter** beyond the baulk line towards the end line (parallel to the midline).
 
• The **Lobby** refers to the **1-meter** wide strips on both sides of the court; these areas are active only after a struggle has commenced between the raider and the defenders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variations in Court Size**:

 
 
• For **Men** and **Senior Boys**, the standard court size is larger, measuring **13 meters × 10 meters**.
 
• For **Sub-Junior Boys and Girls**, the court size is reduced to **11 meters × 8 meters** to accommodate younger athletes.
 
 
 
• **Match Duration**:
 
 
• In the women’s category, a standard match consists of two halves of **15 minutes** each, with a **5-minute interval**.
 
• Men’s matches are longer, featuring two halves of **20 minutes** each.
 
 
 
• **Sitting Block**:
 
 
• This is the area where players who have been 'put out' wait to be revived; for women, this block usually measures **6 meters × 1 meter** and is located outside the end lines.
 
 
 
• **Player Composition**:
 
 
• A team consists of **12 players**, but only **7 players** take the field at the start of the game, while **5 players** remain as substitutes.

questions.question: What main role did the Kaveri River's channels play in Chola period agriculture?

options.text: They provided fertile soil and moisture for crops.
They were used for fishing and boat transportation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They provided fertile soil and moisture for crops**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kaveri River** splits into several small channels before emptying into the **Bay of Bengal**. These channels frequently overflowed, depositing **fertile silt** along their banks.
 
• This deposition of **alluvial soil** was essential for maintaining the productivity of the land, providing a natural fertilizer that supported intensive farming.
 
• The water from these river channels provided the constant **moisture** necessary for agriculture, which was particularly critical for the cultivation of **rice**, the primary staple crop of the region.
 
• During the **Chola period**, the **Kaveri delta** became a hub of agricultural prosperity because the natural flow of these channels was harnessed through systematic **irrigation** techniques.
 
• To control the water flow, **embankments** were built in the delta region to prevent flooding, and **canals** were constructed to carry water directly to the agricultural fields.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chola Irrigation Management**:

 
 
• The **Cholas** were pioneers in water management, building massive **stone dams** and **artificial reservoirs** to store water for the dry seasons.
 
• The **Grand Anicut** (Kallanai), one of the oldest water-regulation structures in the world, was built to divert **Kaveri** waters for irrigation across the delta.
 
• Local **village assemblies** (known as **Sabha** or **Ur**) took an active role in the maintenance of **tanks** and the fair distribution of water among the peasantry.
 
• Agricultural expansion was a state priority, leading to the clearing of **forests** in the **Tamil region** to bring more land under the plow during the **5th and 6th centuries**.
 
• The prosperity generated by this advanced **agro-economic system** provided the surplus wealth needed to build magnificent **Chola temples**, such as the **Brihadisvara Temple** in **Thanjavur**.

questions.question: As of May 2025, who is the Chief Information Commissioner (CIC) of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Heeralal Samariya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Heeralal Samariya** was sworn in as the **Chief Information Commissioner (CIC)** of India on **November 6, 2023**, and continues to hold the office as of **May 2025**.
 
• He is a retired **1985-batch Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** officer of the **Telangana cadre** and was previously serving as an **Information Commissioner** in the **Central Information Commission**.
 
• The oath of office was administered by **President Droupadi Murmu** at **Rashtrapati Bhavan**, following the vacancy created by the retirement of **Yashvardhan Kumar Sinha**.
 
• His appointment is significant as he is the first person from the **Dalit community** to be appointed to the post of **Chief Information Commissioner**.
 
• The selection was made by a high-powered committee chaired by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, including the **Leader of Opposition** in the Lok Sabha and a **Union Cabinet Minister**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Information Commission (CIC)**:

 
 
• The **CIC** is a statutory body established in **2005** under the **Right to Information (RTI) Act** to adjudicate on complaints and appeals regarding information requests.
 
• It consists of a **Chief Information Commissioner** and not more than **ten Information Commissioners**.
 
• Under the **RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019**, the tenure and salaries of the commissioners are determined by the **Central Government**, currently set at **three years** or until the age of **65 years**.
 
 
 
• **Yashvardhan Kumar Sinha**:
 
 
• A former **Indian Foreign Service (IFS)** officer who served as the **11th Chief Information Commissioner** from **2020 to 2023**.
 
 
 
• **Sudhir Bhargava**:
 
 
• A retired **IAS officer** who held the position of the **9th Chief Information Commissioner** from **January 2019 to January 2020**.

questions.question: Under Section 290 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, within how many days from date of framing of charge must an application for plea bargaining be filed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**30**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**, which replaced the **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973**, introduced several procedural reforms to ensure the swift disposal of criminal cases.
 
• **Section 290** of the **BNSS** specifically outlines the procedure for filing an application for **plea bargaining** by an accused person.
 
• According to **Section 290(1)**, an application for **plea bargaining** must be filed within a strict period of **30 days** from the date of **framing of charge**.
 
• This mandatory timeline is a significant addition in the new law, designed to prevent the misuse of **plea bargaining** as a delay tactic during the advanced stages of a trial.
 
• The application must contain a brief description of the case and be accompanied by an **affidavit** sworn by the accused stating that the application is filed **voluntarily**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nature of Plea Bargaining under BNSS**:

 
 
• It is a pre-trial negotiation between the **accused** and the **prosecution** where the accused agrees to plead guilty in exchange for certain concessions.
 
• The provision is applicable only to offenses for which the punishment of **imprisonment** is for a term not exceeding **seven years**.
 
• It excludes offenses that affect the **socio-economic condition** of the country or those committed against a **woman** or a **child** below the age of **fourteen years**.
 
 
 
• **Implementation of BNSS, 2023**:
 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita** received the **Presidential assent** on **December 25, 2023**.
 
• The act came into force on **July 1, 2024**, ushering in a new era of **citizen-centric** and **digitized** criminal justice in India.
 
• The **BNSS** emphasizes **forensic investigation**, **video-conferencing** for trials, and strictly defined **timelines** for various judicial stages.

questions.question: Which chapter of the Part V of the Indian constitution is related with the Executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__I__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part V** of the **Constitution of India** is titled **The Union** and represents the largest part of the Constitution, spanning from **Article 52 to 151**.
 
• **Chapter I** of Part V specifically deals with the **Union Executive**, which includes **Articles 52 to 78**.
 
• The **Union Executive** consists of the **President**, the **Vice-President**, the **Prime Minister**, the **Council of Ministers**, and the **Attorney General for India**.
 
• **Article 52** establishes the office of the **President of India**, while **Article 53** mandates that the **executive power** of the Union shall be vested in the President and exercised either directly or through subordinate officers.
 
• This chapter covers critical aspects such as the **election process**, **eligibility criteria**, **oath or affirmation**, **impeachment procedures**, and the **powers and duties** of the executive branch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Part V of the Constitution is divided into five distinct chapters:
 
 
• **Chapter II**: Focuses on the **Parliament**, covering **Articles 79 to 122**, and details the constitution, officers, and conduct of business in the **Lok Sabha** and **Rajya Sabha**.
 
• **Chapter III**: Relates to the **Legislative Powers of the President**, consisting solely of **Article 123**, which grants the President the power to **promulgate ordinances** during the recess of Parliament.
 
• **Chapter IV**: Pertains to **The Union Judiciary**, encompassing **Articles 124 to 147**, which outline the establishment, jurisdiction, and functions of the **Supreme Court of India**.
 
• **Chapter V**: Governs the **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India (CAG)** via **Articles 148 to 151**, ensuring the accountability of public funds.

questions.question: In which of the following year the Indian National Committee for Space Research grew into ISRO?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1969**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR)** was established in **1962** by the Government of India under the **Department of Atomic Energy (DAE)**.
 
• The committee was formed under the visionary leadership of **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**, who recognized the importance of space research for a developing nation.
 
• On **August 15, 1969**, **INCOSPAR** was superseded by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, marking a significant structural evolution to expand India's space capabilities.
 
• The transition from **INCOSPAR** to **ISRO** institutionalized space activities, moving beyond atmospheric research to the development of **satellite technology** and **launch vehicles**.
 
• This reorganization allowed India to focus on harnessing space science for **telecommunications**, **meteorology**, and **resource management**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Institutional Milestones:**

 
 
• **1972**: The Government of India established the **Space Commission** and the **Department of Space (DOS)**. **ISRO** was brought under the administrative control of **DOS** on **June 1, 1972**.
 
• **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**: Known as the **Father of the Indian Space Program**, he was the first chairman of **INCOSPAR** and played a pivotal role in establishing the **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS)**.
 
• **First Satellite**: Following the formation of **ISRO**, India launched its first indigenous satellite, **Aryabhata**, in **1975** with the assistance of the Soviet Union.
 
 
 
• **Core Objectives of ISRO:**
 
 
• The development of advanced launch systems like the **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** and the **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV)**.
 
• Operation of the **Indian National Satellite (INSAT)** series for broadcasting and the **Indian Remote Sensing (IRS)** satellites for environmental and agricultural monitoring.

questions.question: What is the name of the new light-coloured 'turmeric' variety developed by the Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR), Kozhikode, for the masala industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**IISR Surya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR)**, based in **Kozhikode**, has introduced **IISR Surya**, a specialized variety of **turmeric** designed to meet the specific requirements of the **masala industry**.
 
• This variety is notably distinguished by its **light-coloured rhizomes**, which differ from the traditional deep-orange varieties usually preferred for high curcumin extraction.
 
• **IISR Surya** was developed through rigorous breeding programs aimed at providing a consistent and desirable color profile for **spice blends** and **curry powders** where a milder aesthetic is required.
 
• In addition to its unique color, the variety is characterized by its **high yield potential**, enabling farmers to produce larger quantities to meet the high volume demands of industrial food processors.
 
• The variety ensures an optimal balance of **essential oils** and **oleoresins**, which are critical for maintaining the **aromatic profile** and **flavour integrity** of commercial spice mixtures.
 
• The release of **IISR Surya** addresses a niche market segment in the **spices sector**, focusing on the functional utility of turmeric as a base ingredient in **processed foods** rather than just a source of pigment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **ICAR-Indian Institute of Spices Research (IISR)**:

 
 
• Located in **Kozhikode, Kerala**, it is a premier national institute under the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)**.
 
• It conducts advanced research on various spices including **black pepper**, **cardamom**, **ginger**, and **turmeric** to improve productivity and quality.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric Varieties and Industry Needs**:
 
 
• The **masala industry** often requires specific turmeric grades that do not cause excessive staining but provide the necessary **earthy flavor**.
 
• While varieties like **IISR Pragati** are famous for high **curcumin content** (around 5 percent or more), **IISR Surya** serves the demand for light-coloured, high-volume industrial use.

questions.question: The titled 'Status Report on Child Rights in India: An Overview of the Past Decade', was commissioned as a desk review study by ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Child Rights and You**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The report titled **'Status Report on Child Rights in India: An Overview of the Past Decade'** was commissioned by **Child Rights and You (CRY)** as a comprehensive desk review study to analyze the progress and challenges in the realization of child rights in India.
 
• The study focuses on evaluating the status of children through the lens of four key rights categories defined by the **UN Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC)**: **Right to Survival**, **Right to Development**, **Right to Protection**, and **Right to Participation**.
 
• It utilizes secondary data from significant national sources including the **National Family Health Survey (NFHS)**, **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, **Census of India**, and data from the **National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB)**.
 
• Key findings in the report highlight critical issues such as **malnutrition**, **infant mortality**, the declining **Child Sex Ratio**, and the persistence of **child marriage** and **child labor** despite legislative measures.
 
• The report serves as an advocacy tool for **policymakers** and **civil society** to identify gaps in the implementation of the **Right to Education (RTE) Act** and the **Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Rights and You (CRY)**:

 
 
• Founded in **1979** by **Rippan Kapur**, CRY is an Indian NGO that works to ensure all children have equal opportunities to a childhood.
 
• It focuses on long-term **systemic change** by partnering with local NGOs to address the root causes of child rights violations.
 
 
 
• **Pratham**:
 
 
• An innovative learning organization established in **1995** to improve the quality of education in India.
 
• It is widely recognized for its **Annual Status of Education Report (ASER)**, which tracks children's enrollment and basic learning levels across rural India.
 
 
 
• **Oxfam India**:
 
 
• A non-profit organization that is part of a global confederation dedicated to fighting **inequality** and poverty.
 
• It focuses on areas such as **gender justice**, **health**, **education**, and **economic justice**.
 
 
 
• **SaveLIFE Foundation**:
 
 
• A non-governmental organization focused on improving **road safety** and **emergency medical care** in India.
 
• It was instrumental in the passage of the **Good Samaritan Law** in India to protect bystanders who help crash victims.
